results.title: AI CLOSED-LOOP QUANTUM-NANO FABRICATION AND VERIFICATION AT THE LIMIT Physical Observation × Bounded Decision × Verified Closure This research monograph develops an exploratory engineering architecture for the use of artificial intelligence in nanofabrication workflows where physical evidence, authorization, quality verification, and recovery must remain distinct. Its fundamental claim is modest but consequential: a model-generated recipe proposal should not become an executable manufacturing instruction merely because an optimization objective improved. Every proposed intervention requires a declared physical operating domain, a traceable observation chain, explicit authority, resource and risk bounds, independent verification, and a recoverable failure pathway.
